title: Life Changes
description: Membicarakan perubahan hidup, prestasi, dan kabar terbaru dengan present perfect dan past simple. Kamu akan belajar kapan memakai finished time vs unfinished time, for/since, serta just/already/yet.
objectives: Membedakan present perfect dan past simple berdasarkan finished time dan unfinished time
Menggunakan for dan since untuk menyatakan durasi sampai sekarang
Menggunakan just, already, dan yet untuk kabar terbaru dan rencana yang belum selesai
Menceritakan perubahan hidup dan prestasi pribadi dengan kosakata yang tepat

lessons.title: Present Perfect for Changes and Results
lessons.summary: Mengulang bentuk present perfect dan memakainya untuk pengalaman, perubahan, dan hasil yang terasa sekarang.
objectives: Membentuk present perfect positif, negatif, dan pertanyaan dengan benar
Menggunakan present perfect untuk pengalaman, perubahan, dan hasil sekarang
Menghafal past participle kata kerja tidak beraturan yang umum
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Mengapa present perfect?
Present perfect menghubungkan **masa lalu** dengan **sekarang**. We use it when the exact time is not important, or when a past action has a result now. Di level A2 kamu sudah memakai present perfect untuk pengalaman (*Have you ever...?*). Di B1 kita memperluas pemakaiannya untuk **perubahan** (changes) dan **hasil** (results).

### Bentuk (form)
| Subject | Positive | Negative | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| I / you / we / they | have ('ve) + V3 | haven't + V3 | Have ... + V3? |
| he / she / it | has ('s) + V3 | hasn't + V3 | Has ... + V3? |

V3 = past participle. Regular verbs simply add **-ed** (*change → changed*, *improve → improved*). Irregular verbs harus dihafal: *become → become, grow → grown, lose → lost, write → written, take → taken, buy → bought, go → gone/been*.

### Tiga pemakaian utama
1. **Experience (pengalaman)** — something happened at some time in your life: *I've climbed a volcano.*
2. **Change (perubahan)** — sesuatu berbeda dibandingkan dulu: *My English has improved. The town has grown.*
3. **Result (hasil sekarang)** — aksi di masa lalu, akibatnya terasa sekarang: *I've lost my keys* (= saya tidak punya kunci sekarang). *She's cut her hair* (= rambutnya pendek sekarang).

### Kata kerja untuk perubahan hidup
Verbs like *become, grow, change, improve, get (bigger/better), start, stop* are very common when we talk about life changes. Example: *Dimas has become a father. He has stopped eating fast food and he has started cycling to work.* Semua kalimat ini menjelaskan situasi Dimas **sekarang**, bukan kapan perubahan itu terjadi.

### Hati-hati
- Jangan pakai present perfect dengan waktu lampau yang spesifik (*yesterday, in 2020*). We will compare the two tenses in the next lesson.
- *'s* bisa berarti **is** atau **has**: *She's lost* = She has lost; *She's tired* = She is tired.
- In Indonesian we often use *sudah* or *telah*, but *sudah* does not always mean present perfect. Lihat konteksnya: apakah waktunya disebut? Apakah hasilnya penting sekarang?

sections.summary: Present perfect (**have/has + V3**) connects the past with now. Gunakan untuk **pengalaman**, **perubahan**, dan **hasil yang terasa sekarang**, terutama ketika waktu kejadiannya tidak disebut. Hafalkan past participle yang tidak beraturan seperti become, grown, lost, written.

questions.prompt: Rina looks different today. She ___ her hair short.
questions.explanation: Subject *she* memakai **has**, dan V3 dari *cut* adalah *cut*. The result is visible now: her hair is short.
questions.misconception: Cut adalah irregular verb: cut – cut – cut. Tidak ada bentuk 'cutted'.

questions.prompt: Match each verb with its past participle (V3).
questions.explanation: Irregular past participles harus dihafal: write → written, go → gone, take → taken, buy → bought, grow → grown. They are used in every present perfect sentence.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
questions.explanation: Setelah *has* kita butuh V3. The past participle of *become* is **become**, not *became* (V2).

questions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Pola: subject + has + never + V3. *Never* goes between *has* and the past participle: *Dimas has never lived in a big city.*

lessons.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.summary: Membedakan finished time (past simple) dan unfinished time (present perfect), serta pola percakapan Have you ever...? → When did you...?
objectives: Memilih past simple untuk waktu yang sudah selesai dan disebutkan
Memilih present perfect untuk waktu yang belum selesai atau tidak disebut
Mengikuti pola percakapan: pertanyaan pengalaman lalu pertanyaan detail dengan past simple
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Finished time vs unfinished time
Perbedaan utama antara **past simple** dan **present perfect** adalah *waktu*. Past simple is for a finished time: the period is over, and we often say when it happened. Present perfect is for an unfinished period (today, this week, this year, in my life) or when the time is not mentioned at all.

| Past simple (waktu selesai) | Present perfect (waktu belum selesai / tidak disebut) |
|---|---|
| yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago, when I was a child | today, this week, this year, ever, never, so far, recently |
| *I visited Lombok in 2023.* | *I've visited Lombok three times.* |
| *She wrote two emails yesterday.* | *She has written ten emails today.* |

### Pola percakapan: ever → when/where
Dalam percakapan, kita sering mulai dengan present perfect untuk menanyakan pengalaman, lalu pindah ke past simple untuk detail. Once we know the experience happened, we ask about the specific time, place or details:
- A: *Have you ever been to Port Selwyn?* (pengalaman, waktu tidak penting)
- B: *Yes, I have. I went there last year.* (detail, waktu spesifik)
- A: *What did you do there?* (detail → past simple)

### Today, this morning, this year
Kata seperti *today* atau *this morning* bisa memakai kedua tense, tergantung apakah periodenya sudah selesai. At 10 a.m.: *I've had two coffees this morning* (pagi belum selesai). At 8 p.m.: *I had two coffees this morning* (pagi sudah lewat).

### So far dan recently
*So far* (sejauh ini, sampai sekarang) dan *recently* (baru-baru ini) are typical present perfect signals: *We've sold 200 tickets so far. Have you seen any good films recently?*

### Kesalahan umum orang Indonesia
Karena bahasa Indonesia memakai *sudah* untuk keduanya, learners often say *I have finished it yesterday*. This is wrong: *yesterday* is finished time, so use the **past simple**: *I finished it yesterday.* Juga, pertanyaan dengan **When...?** hampir selalu memakai past simple: *When did you arrive?* (bukan *When have you arrived?*), karena kita menanyakan titik waktu yang spesifik di masa lalu.

lessons.title: For, Since and How Long
lessons.summary: Memakai present perfect dengan for dan since untuk situasi yang dimulai di masa lalu dan masih berlanjut sekarang.
objectives: Bertanya dan menjawab How long have you...?
Membedakan I lived here for... dan I have lived here for...
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### For dan since
Present perfect + **for/since** menjelaskan sesuatu yang dimulai di masa lalu dan **masih berlanjut sampai sekarang**. Bahasa Indonesia biasanya memakai *sudah ... selama* atau *sejak*. Notice the big difference: in English we do NOT use the present simple here. *I live here since 2019* is wrong; say *I have lived here since 2019*.

| for + durasi (period) | since + titik awal (starting point) |
|---|---|
| for ten minutes | since 9 o'clock |
| for three years | since 2021 |
| for a long time / for ages | since last summer |
| for two weeks | since Monday |
| for a decade | since I was a child |

Tip: jika jawabannya "berapa lama?" → **for**. Jika jawabannya "mulai kapan?" → **since**. *Since* can also be followed by a clause in the past simple: *since I moved to Medan*, *since we met*.

### How long...?
Untuk menanyakan durasi, pakai **How long + have/has + subject + V3?**
- *How long have you known Raka?* — *For about five years.* / *Since we were at university.*
- *How long has your sister had her motorbike?* — *Since 2022.*

Jawaban singkat cukup dengan *For...* atau *Since...*.

### Verbs with for/since
State verbs like *know, have, be, like* use the present perfect: *We've known each other for years. I've had this phone since January. She's been a teacher for a decade.* Untuk aktivitas seperti *live, work, study*, present perfect juga benar: *He has worked here for six months.*

### Bandingkan dengan past simple + for
- *I lived in Bandung for five years.* → sudah tidak tinggal di sana (finished).
- *I have lived in Bandung for five years.* → masih tinggal di sana sekarang.

### Ago vs for
*Ago* is different: it goes with the past simple and counts back from now. *I moved here three years ago* memberi informasi yang sama dengan *I have lived here for three years*, tetapi tense-nya berbeda. Never say *since three years* — use **for three years** or **three years ago**.

questions.explanation: *Five years* = durasi → **for**. *March* = titik awal → **since**.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
questions.explanation: *Six years* adalah durasi, jadi harus **for six years**. *Since* hanya untuk titik awal (since 2019).

lessons.title: Just, Already and Yet
lessons.summary: Memakai just, already, dan yet dengan present perfect untuk kabar terbaru, hal yang sudah selesai, dan hal yang belum terjadi.
objectives: Memahami arti just, already, dan yet
Menempatkan just, already, dan yet pada posisi yang benar dalam kalimat
Menjawab pertanyaan dengan Not yet dan memakai still haven't
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Tiga adverb penting
**Just**, **already**, dan **yet** sering muncul bersama present perfect untuk membicarakan berita terbaru dan hal-hal yang kita harapkan terjadi.

| Adverb | Arti | Jenis kalimat | Posisi |
|---|---|---|---|
| just | baru saja | positive | antara *have/has* dan V3 |
| already | sudah (lebih cepat dari dugaan) | positive, juga question | antara *have/has* dan V3, atau di akhir |
| yet | sudah...? / belum | negative & question | di akhir kalimat |

### Just = a very short time ago
*I've just finished my report.* (Saya baru saja menyelesaikan laporan.) *The bus has just left — we missed it!* Use **just** for very recent news.

### Already = sooner than expected / done
*Have you already eaten? It's only 11 o'clock!* *Don't worry, I've already booked the tickets.* **Already** shows that something happened earlier than expected, or that it is done and doesn't need to be done again. Posisi: *I've already paid* atau *I've paid already*.

### Yet = up to now (negatives and questions)
- Question: *Have you finished your homework yet?* (Sudah selesai belum?)
- Negative: *I haven't finished it yet.* (Saya belum menyelesaikannya.)

**Yet** biasanya di **akhir** kalimat. Kita memakai *yet* ketika kita mengharapkan sesuatu akan terjadi.

### Not yet vs still
Jawaban singkat: *Not yet.* (Belum.) **Still** + negative menekankan bahwa kita sudah menunggu lama: *I still haven't heard from Maya* (sampai sekarang pun belum ada kabar, dan saya mulai khawatir). Note the position: *still* comes **before** *haven't/hasn't*.

### Catatan untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia
*Sudah* bisa berarti *already* atau tidak perlu diterjemahkan: *Sudah makan?* → *Have you eaten (yet)?* *Belum.* → *Not yet.* Remember: don't use *yet* in positive sentences (*I have finished yet* ✗), and don't use *already* in negative sentences to mean *belum* (*I haven't paid already* ✗ → *I haven't paid yet* ✓).

mistakes.wrong: I have finished yet my homework.
mistakes.right: I have already finished my homework.
mistakes.why: Yet tidak dipakai di kalimat positif; gunakan already.

mistakes.wrong: I haven't paid the bill already.
mistakes.right: I haven't paid the bill yet.
mistakes.why: Untuk arti 'belum' gunakan yet di akhir kalimat negatif.

mistakes.right: She has just finished the project.
mistakes.why: Just diletakkan di antara has dan V3.

mistakes.wrong: I haven't still called her.
mistakes.right: I still haven't called her.
mistakes.why: Still diletakkan sebelum haven't/hasn't.

sections.summary: **Just** = baru saja, **already** = sudah (sooner than expected), **yet** = sudah? / belum in questions and negatives. Just and already go between *have/has* and the past participle; yet usually goes at the end. Jawaban singkat untuk 'belum' adalah *Not yet*.

reviewCards.back: sudah (lebih cepat dari dugaan) — She's already left.
Have you eaten yet? (sudah belum?) / I haven't eaten yet. (belum)
Sebelum haven't/hasn't: I still haven't finished.

questions.explanation: Kalimat negatif dengan arti 'belum' → **yet** di akhir kalimat. *Already* and *just* are used in positive sentences.

questions.explanation: Pola pertanyaan: Have + subject + V3 + object + **yet**? *Yet* goes at the end: *Have you sent the email to Mr. Hartono yet?*

questions.prompt: You are moving to a new flat next week. Your friend asks: "Are you ready for the move?" Answer in 3–5 sentences. Say what you have already done, what you have just done, and what you haven't done yet.
questions.sampleAnswer: Almost! I've already packed my books and clothes. I've just booked a van for Saturday. But I haven't told my landlord yet, and I still haven't found a new desk.
questions.explanation: Gunakan **already** dan **just** di kalimat positif (antara have dan V3), dan **yet** di akhir kalimat negatif. Try to sound natural with contractions: *I've, I haven't*.

questions.prompt: A: Is Lina still at the office? B: No, she ___ left. You missed her by two minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Two minutes' ago = very recent → **has just** left. *Just* goes between *has* and the past participle; *yet* is not used in positive sentences.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence using the word given.
questions.explanation: *Already* biasanya diletakkan di antara *have* dan V3 (**have already arrived**), atau di akhir kalimat.

questions.prompt: Translate into Indonesian.
questions.source: I haven't paid the bill yet.
questions.explanation: *Haven't ... yet* = **belum**. *The bill* = tagihan(nya).

lessons.title: Recent News and Achievements
lessons.summary: Bertukar kabar tentang perubahan hidup dan prestasi: headline dengan present perfect, detail dengan past simple.
objectives: Menggunakan kosakata perubahan hidup (graduate, get promoted, move house, settle down, retire)
Menyampaikan kabar dengan present perfect lalu detail dengan past simple
Merespons kabar baik dan buruk dengan ungkapan yang tepat
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi, selesaikan latihan menulis, dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Talking about life changes
Ketika bertemu teman lama, kita sering bertukar kabar. Typical questions are *What's new? How are things? I haven't seen you for ages!* We usually answer with the **present perfect** for the news "headline", then switch to the **past simple** for the details.

### Headline → details
| Headline (present perfect) | Details (past simple) |
|---|---|
| *I've got a new job!* | *I started last month. I had three interviews.* |
| *Sinta has moved house.* | *She moved to Port Selwyn in March.* |
| *We've got engaged!* | *Bayu proposed on the beach last Saturday.* |

Pola ini sama seperti berita di TV atau media sosial: kalimat pertama memberi kabar (present perfect), kalimat berikutnya menjelaskan kapan, di mana, dan bagaimana (past simple).

### Life-change vocabulary
- **graduate (from)** — lulus dari universitas/sekolah: *She graduated from university in June.*
- **get promoted** — naik jabatan: *He's just got promoted to manager.*
- **move house** — pindah rumah
- **settle down** — hidup menetap dan tenang, biasanya menikah dan punya rumah sendiri
- **get engaged / get married** — bertunangan / menikah
- **retire** — pensiun
- **start a business** — memulai usaha
- **pass an exam / a driving test** — lulus ujian

### Reacting to news
Untuk merespons kabar, pakai ungkapan yang sesuai: *Congratulations!* (good news, especially weddings, babies, new jobs), *That's great news!*, *Well done!* (for an achievement like passing an exam), *Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that.* (bad news). Then ask a follow-up question in the past simple: *When did it happen? How did you feel?*

### Achievements
Kata **achievement** (prestasi) dan verb **achieve** sering dipakai dengan present perfect karena hidup kita belum selesai: *What is your biggest achievement? — I've run a marathon.* You can also use *so far*: *I've visited five countries so far.* Tetapi jika kamu menyebut waktu, kembali ke past simple: *I ran my first marathon in 2022.*

Andi has got promoted to team leader.
We've moved house three times.
After years of travelling, he has finally settled down.

Mrs. Wulan retired last year.

grammar.example: I took it yesterday in Port Selwyn.
Congratulations! When did you hear the news?

mistakes.wrong: I've graduated university last year.
mistakes.right: I graduated from university last year.
mistakes.why: Last year → past simple; gunakan graduate from.

mistakes.wrong: He has promoted to manager.
mistakes.right: He has got promoted to manager.
mistakes.why: Untuk arti 'naik jabatan' gunakan get promoted.

mistakes.wrong: We moved home last month to a new house.
mistakes.right: We moved house last month.
mistakes.why: Ungkapan yang umum adalah move house (pindah rumah).

mistakes.wrong: Congratulation!
mistakes.right: Congratulations!
mistakes.why: Ucapan selamat selalu memakai -s.

sections.summary: Share news with the **present perfect** (*I've got a new job!*) and give details with the **past simple** (*I started last week*). Pelajari kosakata perubahan hidup seperti graduate, get promoted, move house, settle down, get engaged, dan retire, lalu respons kabar dengan *Congratulations!* atau *I'm sorry to hear that.*

reviewCards.back: Headline: present perfect (I've moved!) → Details: past simple (I moved in May)
Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that.

questions.prompt: Match each expression with its Indonesian meaning.
questions.explanation: Kosakata perubahan hidup: *get promoted* = naik jabatan, *move house* = pindah rumah, *settle down* = hidup menetap, *graduate* = lulus, *retire* = pensiun.

questions.prompt: Mrs. Wulan worked as a teacher for 35 years. Last month she ___, and now she has a lot of free time.
questions.explanation: Berhenti bekerja setelah 35 tahun dan sekarang punya banyak waktu luang → **retired** (pensiun). *Graduated* is for finishing university.

questions.prompt: Write a short message to a friend you haven't seen for a long time. Tell them about two or three changes in your life. Give the news with the present perfect and the details with the past simple.
questions.instructions: Tulis 60–110 kata. Gunakan minimal satu dari: just, already, yet, for, since.
questions.explanation: Contoh: *Hi Dimas! I haven't seen you for ages. A lot has changed! I've moved house — I moved to Port Selwyn in March. I've also got a new job at a travel agency. I started two weeks ago and I've already made some good friends there...* Use the present perfect for headlines and the past simple for details.

questions.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order to make a message.
questions.explanation: Headline dengan present perfect (*has just got promoted*), lalu detail dengan past simple + waktu (*moved ... on Monday*).

questions.prompt: Tari and Bayu ___ last month! They're getting married next June.
questions.explanation: Mereka akan menikah bulan Juni → bulan lalu mereka **got engaged** (bertunangan).

questions.prompt: Choose the best line to complete the conversation.

dialogue.speaker: Fajar
dialogue.text: Hi Sinta! I haven't seen you for ages. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Sinta
dialogue.text: Last week. The ceremony was on Saturday.

options: I graduate from university next year.
questions.explanation: Kabar baru (headline) memakai present perfect: **I've just graduated**. Fajar's reply (*Congratulations! When did you finish?*) shows the event is already finished.

unitTestQuestions.explanation: Pertanyaan **When...?** menanyakan waktu spesifik di masa lalu → past simple: *When did you get your first job?*

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: Lestari ___ (work) as a journalist for eight years, and she still loves her job. She ___ (write) her first article in 2017.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Masih bekerja sampai sekarang + for eight years → **has worked**. *In 2017* adalah finished time → past simple **wrote**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Correct the mistake in the question.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Setelah *have* kita butuh V3. *Went* adalah V2; V3 yang tepat adalah **been** (pengalaman) — *Have you ever been abroad?*

unitTestQuestions.source: Saya sudah tinggal di Medan sejak tahun 2019.
answers: I have lived in Medan since 2019
I have been living in Medan since 2019
I've been living in Medan since 2019
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Situasi dari 2019 sampai sekarang → present perfect + **since**: *I have lived in Medan since 2019.* Jangan pakai *I live in Medan since 2019*.

unitTestQuestions.text: A: Has the parcel arrived? B: No, not ___. But the courier has ___ called — he'll be here in ten minutes.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Not yet* = belum. *Has just called* = baru saja menelepon. *Yet* tidak dipakai di kalimat positif, dan *for* tidak cocok di sini.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Which sentences are correct? Choose all that apply.
options: I've known Raka since we were twelve.
She has moved house last year.
Have you finished your project yet?
We got married five years ago.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Benar: *since we were twelve* (titik awal), *yet* di akhir pertanyaan, dan *five years ago* + past simple. Salah: *has moved ... last year* (harus *moved*), *for 2010* (harus *since 2010*).

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
fragments: I have had four different jobs,
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Since I left school* + present perfect (*have had*) untuk periode sampai sekarang; *last month* + past simple (*started*) untuk waktu spesifik.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the question.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Durasi sampai sekarang memakai present perfect: **How long have you known** your best friend Kevin? Present simple is wrong here.
